dct_description_sm: We evaluated the global distribution of cyanobacteria by comparing communities from the most northern reaches of North America (Canadian High Arctic) with those from analogous sites in Antarctica. We determined the diversity and community structure of cyanobacterial mats collected from lakes, ponds and streams on land, and from meltwater lakes on ice shelves, at the northern limit of the North American Arctic, specifically Ward Hunt Island (latitude 83.11N) and its vicinity in Quttinirpaaq ('top of the world' in Inuktitut) National Park, Nunavut, Canada. Cyanobacterial diversity was determined in the microbial mats by way of morphological characters, 16S rRNA gene similarity and pigment biomarkers. Additional work is being undertaken on the viruses associated with High Arctic cyanobacteria.
dct_title_s: Diversity, activity and biogeography of cyanobacteria in Canadian High Arctic
